newsitem.title: USA: Magnesium shipments remain at high levels - IMA.
newsitem.headline: Magnesium shipments remain at high levels - IMA.

text.p: Global primary magnesium shipments totaled 75,500 tonnes in the second quarter of 1996, down 1,400 tonnes from 1995's record second quarter, the International Magnesium Association reported.
First half shipments of 150,600 tonnes were off 1,800 tonnes.

First half shipments comprised 115,800 tonnes of production from Brazil, Canada, France, Norway and the U.S., plus estimated exports of 34,800 tonnes from the Commonwealth of Independent States and China.
Inventories recovered to 33,400 tonnes from their record low of 17,200 tonnes on June 30 1995, with 3,100 tonnes being added during the second quarter of 1996.

First half shipments of magnesium to the aluminum alloying sector fell 9,100 tonnes to 72,300 tonnes, while shipments to the desulfurizing market - where magnesium is used to purify steel - were up 4,800 tonnes to 20,600 tonnes.
The rise in desulfurization was "probably reflecting a switch away from scrap and some inventory rebuilding," the IMA said.
Shipments to the diecasting sector rose 2,200 tonnes to 33,100 tonnes.
First half production totaled 126,400 tonnes, up 6,100 tonnes on last year. First half production in the U.S. and Canada totaled 97,100 tonnes, up from 93,700 tonnes in the same period last year.
